lines.japanese: 次の休み時間、僕は思うところあって席を立った。
lines.english: At the next break, a thought prompted me to leave my seat.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、さっきの話なんだけど」
lines.english: “Watarai, about what we were discussing earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、結婚式は和洋どっちがいいかって話？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, whether we should have a Japanese or Western wedding?”

lines.japanese: 「そんな話はしてないよ、面白い深夜アニメの話だよ」
lines.english: “We weren't discussing that. We were discussing good late-night anime.”

lines.japanese: 「わあ、マジレスとしてはなかなかサイアクな部類だね」
lines.english: “Wow. As ways of taking a joke seriously go, that was about the worst.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、ＤＶＤレコーダーのセッティングするって話。良かったら今日、病院の帰りにちょっと渡来さんち寄っていこうか？」
lines.english: “Actually, I mean setting up your DVD recorder. If you want, I could stop at your place for a little while after we leave the hospital today.”

lines.japanese: 今日は放課後、ふたりで森里君のお見舞いへ行く予定だった。
lines.english: Watarai and I planned to visit Morisato after school today.

lines.japanese: 「や、とくに急いでないから、週末とか時間あるときでいいよ」
lines.english: “There's no hurry. This weekend or whenever you have time is fine.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？　急いだ方がいいと思うけどなあ。渡来さんにお勧めの作品、他にもいくつかあるんだ」
lines.english: “Really? I think we should hurry. There are several other shows I'd like to recommend to you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああそう」
lines.english: “O-Oh, really.”

lines.japanese: 「本とか映画で渡来さんの好みはけっこう分かってきたから、そんなに外れたりはしないと思うよ」
lines.english: “I'm starting to understand your tastes in books and movies, so I don't think my choices will miss by much.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう？」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: 「今日だったら、水曜だから『ゆりかごの堕天使はモザイク越しの前戯を嗤う』かな。流行りの学園異能バトルものなんだけど、背景カットを多用して無機質な心情を描写する独特の演出が──」
lines.english: “Since today's Wednesday, there's *The Cradle's Fallen Angel Laughs at Foreplay Through the Mosaic*. It's one of the popular supernatural school battle shows, but it has a distinctive direction style that uses lots of background cuts to portray an inorganic state of mind—”

lines.japanese: あ。
lines.english: Oh.

lines.japanese: しばしば指摘される自分の悪い癖に思いあたって、僕はそこで口をつぐんだ。
lines.english: I remembered a bad habit people often pointed out and closed my mouth there.

lines.japanese: いろんなひとが教えてくれた。自分の言いたいことを一方的に発しつづけるだけじゃ駄目なんだ。
lines.english: Many people had taught me this. I couldn't simply keep broadcasting whatever I wanted to say in one direction.

lines.japanese: 「……うん、まあ、そんな感じ」
lines.english: “...Well, that's the general idea.”
“Oh?”

lines.japanese: 僕が言葉を止めると、渡来さんはちょっと驚いていた。
lines.english: When I stopped talking, Watarai looked a little surprised.

lines.japanese: くいくい、と人差し指で手招きされる。
lines.english: She beckoned me closer with a curl of her index finger.

lines.japanese: なんだろう。耳を貸そうと腰を折ったら、頭を撫でられてしまった。飼い主と犬。
lines.english: What was it? I bent down to lend her my ear, only for her to pat my head. Owner and dog.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ、観るよ」
lines.english: “Fine. I'll watch it.”

lines.japanese: 抗議しようと思ったら、意外と優しい反応があって士気を挫かれてしまう。
lines.english: I was about to protest when her unexpectedly kind response sapped my fighting spirit.

lines.japanese: 「いつやってんの？　ケータイに入れとく」
lines.english: “When is it on? I'll put it in my phone.”

lines.japanese: 「え……いや、そんな、無理しなくても」
lines.english: “What...? No, you don't have to force yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「無理とかじゃないよ。羽田君だって、私の好きなマイナー音楽とか聴いてくれるじゃん」
lines.english: “I'm not forcing myself. You listen to obscure music I like too, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……うん、好きなひとが好きなものって、なんか特別な感じするんだ」
lines.english: “Oh... Yes. Something a person you love also loves feels special somehow.”

lines.japanese: それのどんなところが好きなのか、どういう想いでそれに触れているのか。そういったことを考えながら作品を味わうと、とても温かな気持ちになれるんだ。
lines.english: What did she love about it? What feelings did it evoke when she experienced it? Enjoying a work while thinking about those things could fill me with a wonderful warmth.

lines.japanese: 「分かる。それだよ」
lines.english: “I understand. That's exactly it.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが携帯電話のスケジュール帳を開いた。僕はちょっと照れながら、もう一度そのタイトルと、詳しい放映時間とを説明した。
lines.english: Watarai opened the calendar on her cell phone. A little embarrassed, I repeated the title and gave her the exact broadcast time.

lines.japanese: 「演出のひとが今回は古き良きフランス映画を意識しててね。渡来さん好きだったでしょ、そういうの。絵柄もさっぱりしてて一般向けだし、全体的にメジャー志向の……そうだ、主題歌が御影クリヤだった」
lines.english: “The director was consciously imitating classic French cinema this time. You like that kind of thing, don't you? The clean art style is accessible, and the whole production is aimed at a more mainstream... Oh, right. Kuriya Mikage sings the theme song.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、栗山君」
lines.english: “Oh, Kuriyama.”
“Who's that?”

lines.japanese: コア層向けじゃないってことをアピールしたくて、邦楽トップアーティストの名前を出したのだけど伝わらなかった。そういえば前にもこんなことがあった気がする。
lines.english: I had mentioned a chart-topping Japanese artist to show her that the series wasn't only for hardcore fans, but the name meant nothing to her. Come to think of it, I felt as though this had happened before.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、あの子いまは成り行きで耽美キャラ気取ってるけど、元来プラモデルとかカードゲームの好きな子だったからね。アニメのタイアップなんて本人喜んでると思うよ」
lines.english: “Well, that boy puts on this decadent-aesthete act because of how things worked out, but he originally loved model kits and card games. I bet he's thrilled about an anime tie-in.”

lines.japanese: 誰と間違ってるんだろう。まるで昔の同級生を懐かしんでいるみたいな口振りだ。
lines.english: Who was she confusing him with? She sounded as though she were reminiscing about an old classmate.

lines.japanese: 「違うよ渡来さん、ロックバードのボーカルだった御影──」
lines.english: “No, Watarai. I mean Mikage, the former vocalist of Rockbird—”

lines.japanese: 「──ＫｕＲｉＹａの話？」
lines.english: “—You're talking about KuRiYa?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes.”

lines.japanese: するっと入ってきた山科さんだけど、ライブにまで出向くほどクリヤ好きな彼女の目は静かに輝いていた。
lines.english: Yamashina slipped into the conversation. She liked KuRiYa enough to go to his concerts, and her eyes shone quietly.

lines.japanese: 「山科さんなら知ってるよね、御影クリヤが『ゆりかごの堕天使はモザイク越しの前戯を嗤う』のオープニングテーマ歌ってるの」
lines.english: “You know about it, Yamashina, don't you? Kuriya Mikage sings the opening theme for *The Cradle's Fallen Angel Laughs at Foreplay Through the Mosaic*.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いいよね『ゆりモザ』。あの空気は好きだな」
lines.english: “Oh, *Cradle Mosaic*. It's good. I like that atmosphere.”

lines.japanese: 「山科も観てんの？」
lines.english: “You watch it too, Yamashina?”

lines.japanese: 「主題歌から入ったんだけど、作品も良かった。面白かったっていうより、うん、良かった」
lines.english: “The theme song drew me in, but the show itself was good too. I wouldn't call it entertaining exactly. Just... good.”

lines.japanese: 「そう、それなんだよ。いいこと言うなあ山科さん。こないだ７話がネットでいろいろ言われてたけど、おれは熱い戦闘シーンだけが『ゆりモザ』じゃないと思うんだ」
lines.english: “Yes, that's it. Well put, Yamashina. Episode seven got a lot of criticism online, but I don't think *Cradle Mosaic* is only about heated battle scenes.”

lines.japanese: 「あの監督、話が膠着してるときほど見せ方が叙情的になるから、バトル派にはなおさら退屈なんだろうね」
lines.english: “That director gets more lyrical with the visuals whenever the story stalls, so of course the battle fans find it especially boring.”

lines.japanese: 「ああいうところでキャラの人間っぽさを丁寧に描いてるからこそ、命を懸けた戦いが感動的なものになってると思うんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “But it's the care those scenes take in portraying the characters as human beings that makes their battles to the death so moving.”

lines.japanese: 「私は、３話だっけ？　ロングの構図でゆっくり河原をなめていくシーンで涙腺ゆるんだ」
lines.english: “Was it episode three? The long shot that slowly panned across the riverbank made me tear up.”

lines.japanese: 「そう！　あそこはＢＧＭもずるいよね、あれ１話で初めて出撃したときのバージョン違いだもん」
lines.english: “Exactly! The music there is unfair too. It's a variation on the piece from their first sortie in episode one.”

lines.japanese: 「他にも何パターンかサントラに入ってるよね。どんな使い方されるのか、いまから楽しみ……」
lines.english: “There are several other arrangements on the soundtrack. I'm already looking forward to hearing how they use them...”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんは最近どんなテレビ観てる？」
lines.english: “What have you been watching lately, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: とつぜん山科さんが話題を変えた。
lines.english: Yamashina abruptly changed the subject.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。そうだよね。
lines.english: Oh. Of course. She was right.

lines.japanese: こういうところが、僕は空気を読めないと言われる所以なんだ。
lines.english: Moments like this were why people told me I couldn't read the room.

lines.japanese: 山科さんが席へ戻っていったあと、僕は渡来さんに謝った。
lines.english: After Yamashina returned to her seat, I apologized to Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「さっきはふたりで勝手に盛りあがっちゃってごめんね」
lines.english: “Sorry we got carried away talking to each other.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　いいよ、そんなの。ぜんぜん気にしないで」
lines.english: “Huh? It's fine. Don't worry about it at all.”

lines.japanese: 「私は楽しそうな彼氏を見て勝手に楽しむから」
lines.english: “I’m happy just watching my boyfriend have fun.”

lines.japanese: ありがとう。僕の彼女はとても心の広いひとなんだ。
lines.english: Thank you. My girlfriend was an extraordinarily generous person.

lines.japanese: 今日の授業はぜんぶ終わった。
lines.english: The day's classes finally ended.

lines.japanese: このあとは渡来さんとふたりで、森里君のお見舞いだ。
lines.english: Now Watarai and I would visit Morisato together.

lines.japanese: いまの僕は彼の存在を意識するとき、同時に成田隼人としての印象や経験をも≪思いだす≫けれど、さりとて僕は僕だ。
lines.english: Whenever I thought of him now, I simultaneously ≪remembered≫ my impressions and experiences as Hayato Narita. Even so, I was myself.

lines.japanese: かつて成田君だった僕が、たとえ森里君をどう思っていたとしても。たとえ何を知っていたとしても──
lines.english: Whatever the person I once was as Narita might have thought of Morisato. Whatever he might have known—

lines.japanese: ──それは羽田タカシが築いてきた森里和馬への友愛の情を制限するものには成りえなかった。
lines.english: —none of it could constrain the friendship that Takashi Haneda had built with Kazuma Morisato.

lines.japanese: だから僕は思わない。彼の自慢の長い髪が、ウザくてキモくて鬱陶しいだなんて。
lines.english: That was why I did not think his prized long hair was annoying, gross, or obnoxious.

lines.japanese: たぶん。
lines.english: Probably.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせー。かーえろ」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting. Let's go home.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 下校準備を終えた渡来さんが、僕の席まで迎えにきてくれた。
lines.english: Watarai, ready to leave, came to collect me at my desk.

lines.japanese: いっしょに帰りはじめた当初は、周囲から冷やかしやら何やらの声をさんざん浴びせかけられたけど、もうそろそろみんな飽きてきたみたいだ。
lines.english: When we first started leaving school together, everyone had teased us mercilessly. By now, though, they seemed to be getting tired of it.

lines.japanese: きょう僕らの前に立ちふさがったのはひとり。
lines.english: Only one person blocked our way today.

lines.japanese: 「羽田」
lines.english: “Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、針生さん。今日、学校来てたんですか？　朝から姿を見ませんでしたけど」
lines.english: “Oh, Hariu. You were at school today? I haven’t seen you all day.”

lines.japanese: 「まさか一日保健室にいたとか？」
lines.english: “Don't tell me you spent the whole day in the nurse's office.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、応接室で学園長に将棋の指南してた。ン、これ口外禁止か？」
lines.english: “No, I was in the reception room instructing the headmaster in shogi. Mm. Was that confidential?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、たぶん……」
lines.english: “Um, probably...”

lines.japanese: つくづく謎の多いひとだ。
lines.english: He truly was a man of endless mysteries.

lines.japanese: 「そんなことより羽田、『いもももと』はどうだ」
lines.english: “More importantly, Haneda, what do you think of *Imomomoto*?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、面白そうですよね」
lines.english: “Oh, it looks interesting.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なんて？　いももと？」
lines.english: “Huh? What was that? *Imomoto*?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ渡来さん、いもももとだよ。来週発売の恋愛ゲーム。攻略可ヒロインがぜんぶ妹キャラなんだ」
lines.english: “No, Watarai. *Imomomoto*. It's a romance game coming out next week. Every heroine you can pursue is a little-sister character.”

lines.japanese: 「あたー、先輩そっち行っちゃったんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh, man. You went over to that side, huh, Hariu...?”

lines.japanese: 「さァて、そいつはどうだろうなァ」
lines.english: “Well now. Did I?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、行ってんでしょ。明らかに好きなんでしょ。なに謎多き男みたいな顔してんの」
lines.english: “You obviously did. You obviously love it. Quit making that mysterious-man face.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でもね渡来さん、妹萌えは好きっていう感情と必ずしもイコールじゃないんだ。とくに実妹キャラの場合、異性としてではなく、実の家族に対するような愛情を持つこともあってね」
lines.english: “But Watarai, the appeal of little-sister characters isn’t necessarily romantic. With biological-sister characters in particular, the feeling can be affection for actual family rather than for the opposite sex.”

lines.japanese: 「詳しいな」
lines.english: “You sure know a lot.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、それはどうだろうねえ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Do I?”

lines.japanese: 「うわー、こいつらめんどくせぇー」
lines.english: “God, you two are a pain in the ass.”

lines.japanese: 「でもなァ、正味な話、ひとつのカテゴリーとして括るにはいささか強引が過ぎるんだよなァ」
lines.english: “But seriously, grouping all of them as one category is forcing it a little too far.”

lines.japanese: 「たしかに『実妹』『義妹』『従姉妹』『男の娘的な弟』ぐらいまではまだしも『妹的存在』はただの他人だろ、なんて批判も多いですよね」
lines.english: “Exactly. Biological sisters, stepsisters, cousins, and even feminine little brothers are one thing. But lots of people point out that a ‘little-sister-like presence’ is just some unrelated girl.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ妹萌えってなァ、家族としての異質な距離があって初めて成立する概念だからなァ。実妹にせよ義妹にせよ、背徳感はマストでしょう」
lines.english: “The appeal of little-sister characters only exists because of that strange distance within a family. Biological or otherwise, a sense of transgression is mandatory.”

lines.japanese: 「でも禁忌であることが強調されすぎると、精神的葛藤の描写が多くなってプリミティブな萌えが阻害されてしまいますよね。そういう意味じゃ、おれは義妹の方がポテンシャルは高いのかなって思うんですけど」
lines.english: “But if the taboo gets emphasized too much, you end up with so much inner conflict that it gets in the way of that basic heart-melting appeal. In that sense, I think stepsisters may have the higher potential.”

lines.japanese: 「砂漠のラクダと氷原のトナカイ、いずれが有益か競うことに意義はあるか？　やめなよ、実妹と義妹はもはや別ジャンルだ」
lines.english: “Is there value in asking whether a camel in the desert or a reindeer on the ice is more useful? Stop it. Biological and stepsisters are already separate genres.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですね。いや、参りました。まさかこのおれが、針生さんから教えられる日が来ようとは……あ」
lines.english: “You're right. I concede defeat. To think the day would come when I learned something from you, Hariu... Oh.”

lines.japanese: 突然、ふと、我に返った。
lines.english: Without warning, I came to my senses.

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、すみません針生さん。おれたち、いまから友達のお見舞いに行くところなんです」
lines.english: “Right. Sorry, Hariu. We're on our way to visit a friend in the hospital.”

lines.japanese: 学習していた僕は、渡来さんの参加できない話をそこで切りあげた。
lines.english: Having learned my lesson, I ended the conversation Watarai couldn't participate in.

lines.japanese: 針生さんと別れて教室を出たあと、僕は渡来さんに謝った。
lines.english: After we parted with Hariu and left the classroom, I apologized to Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「さっきはふたりで勝手に盛りあがっちゃってごめんね」
lines.english: “Sorry we got carried away talking to each other.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、いいよ。あんまりは気にしないで。うん、あんまりはね」
lines.english: “No, it’s fine. Don’t worry about it *too* much. Right. Not *too* much.”

lines.japanese: ありがとう。僕の彼女はとても心の広いひとなんだ。
lines.english: Thank you. My girlfriend was an extraordinarily generous person.

lines.japanese: 森里君がお世話になってる病院は駅の反対側、花水木通り沿いの外れにある。
lines.english: The hospital treating Morisato stood across the station, near the far end of Flowering Dogwood Street.

lines.japanese: すでに何度かお邪魔しているので、おみやげはもう勘弁してもらっていた。まだ学生の僕には、ちょっとしたフルーツ代の節約も馬鹿にならない。
lines.english: We had already intruded on him several times, so he had finally excused us from bringing gifts. As a student, I couldn't dismiss even the cost of a little fruit.

lines.japanese: 以前は千歳君だった僕や、成田君だった僕が、身を粉にしてアルバイトしてくれていたけれど、いまは受験に集中することを理由にすべて休業させてもらっていた。
lines.english: The versions of me who had once been Chitose and Narita had worked themselves to the bone at part-time jobs, but now I had put them all on hold so I could concentrate on entrance exams.

lines.japanese: 休職を願いでるとき、アレキサンダーの軽部店長や祥玄社の米田編集、それから工事現場の重田主任やパルクレープの春日さんといった、僕ではない僕の恩人たちに頭を下げてまわった。
lines.english: When I requested leave, I made the rounds bowing to the benefactors of my other selves: Manager Karube at Alexander, Editor Yoneda at Shougensha, Foreman Shigeta at the construction site, and Kasuga at Paru Crêpes.

lines.japanese: その折には、たくさんの愉快なひとびとと「初めて再会」することができた。
lines.english: In the process, I was able to ‘meet again for the first time’ with a great many delightful people.

lines.japanese: 中でも、成田君のお友達のこの子は、ふわっとして地に足の付かないところが僕と似ている気がした。
lines.english: Of them all, this friend of Narita's seemed rather like me in her airy way of never quite having her feet on the ground.

lines.japanese: 「あー、ドラさん彼女連れですかー、熱いよ熱いよひゅーひゅー」
lines.english: “Ooh, Dora brought his girlfriend. Hot stuff! Woo-hoo!”

lines.japanese: 白々しく囃したてる彼女は、鳳鳴さん。春日さんの店で出会った、パルクレープの常連客。
lines.english: The girl cheering us on with theatrical insincerity was Naru Ohtori, a Paru Crêpes regular whom I had met at Kasuga's shop.

lines.japanese: ストイックな成田隼人君のイメージがよほど強いみたいで、あの界隈のひとたちは、ほとんどが僕と渡来さんの関係を信じていなかった。
lines.english: The people in that circle had such a strong image of the stoic Hayato Narita that almost none of them believed Watarai and I were together.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いんじゃない。とくに不都合ないし」
lines.english: “Well, that's fine. It doesn't cause any problems.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんがそう言うので、僕もとくに強調することはしなかった。たぶん照れもあったんだろう。
lines.english: Since Watarai said that, I didn't go out of my way to insist. I was probably embarrassed too.

lines.japanese: 「鳳さんも放課後の寄り道？」
lines.english: “Are you making a stop after school too, Ohtori?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ちょっと本屋さんでも見ていこうかとー」
lines.english: “Yes. I thought I'd browse a bookstore.”

lines.japanese: 「鳳さんってどんな本読むの？」
lines.english: “What kind of books do you read?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、そうですねー、小説だったら恋愛ものとかー。ノンフィクションだったら女流作家のエッセイとかー」
lines.english: “Hmm. Romance, if it's fiction. Essays by women writers, if it's nonfiction.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、流行りの作家で言うと、白金台あざぶ子とか代官山えびす子とか？」
lines.english: “Then among fashionable writers, Azabuko Shirokanedai or Ebisuko Daikanyama?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そーですその辺です、午後のオープンカフェで開いてるとデキる女に見えちゃう系のアレですー」
lines.english: “Yes, exactly, that sort! The kind that makes you look like an accomplished woman if you open it at an outdoor cafe in the afternoon.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ愛田保ぽてとの『二階からパティスリー』なんかもお勧めだよ」
lines.english: “Then I’d recommend Potato Idaho’s *Patisserie from the Second Floor* too.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー！　なんで私の好み知ってるんですかー！　それもー擦りきれそうなほど読みまくりましたよ、午後のオープンカフェでー！」
lines.english: “What?! How did you know what I like? I've read that until the pages are nearly worn through—at an outdoor cafe in the afternoon!”

lines.japanese: 「あとは多摩いづみさんの『青春はそれを我慢できない』も読んでほしいかな。まあ、その系統の本に敏感なブログがあって、そこの管理人はさわこさんって言うんだけど──」
lines.english: “I'd also like you to read Tama Izumi's *Youth Can't Resist It*. There's a blog that's very alert to books in that vein, and its owner is a woman named Sawako—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、ごめんね鳳さん。おれたち、いまから森里君のお見舞いに行くところなんだ」
lines.english: “—Oh, sorry, Ohtori. We're on our way to visit Morisato in the hospital.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そうだったんですかー。じゃー、痛んだ髪お大事にとお伝えくださいー」
lines.english: “Oh, were you? Then tell him to take care of his damaged hair.”

lines.japanese: 鳳さんが去っていったあと、僕は渡来さんに謝った。
lines.english: After Ohtori left, I apologized to Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「さっきはふたりで勝手に盛りあがっちゃってごめんね」
lines.english: “Sorry we got carried away talking to each other.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ、そういう日もあるよね。べつに、ものすごくは気にしないで。そんな、ものすごくって程は気にしないでいいから。うん、ホントそこまでは気にしなくてもいいんだけど、まーまー臨機応変にね」
lines.english: “Well, we all have days like that. Don’t worry yourself sick over it. There’s no need to worry *that* much. Really, not that much, but... use your judgment, okay?”

lines.japanese: ありがとう。僕の彼女はとても心の広いひとなんだ。
lines.english: Thank you. My girlfriend was an extraordinarily generous person.

lines.japanese: そして僕らは森里君の病室を訪れた。
lines.english: Then we entered Morisato's hospital room.

lines.japanese: 「くたばれ、ドラゴン野郎！　おるァ、必殺ペガサス斬りィィィ！」
lines.english: “Drop dead, dragon bastard! Take this—ultimate Pegasus Slaaash!”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、だめだよ森里君。そんな無茶苦茶に暴れないで、まずは角を破壊しないと報酬が……」
lines.english: “Wait, Morisato. Don't flail around like that. You need to break the horns first or the reward—”

lines.japanese: 「そんでェ、そのあと三番目に出てきたのが四中で五番目に強ええ三島ってヤローなんだけど、俺はその一月前に六中で四番目に強ええ三連パンチの一郎を二発で沈めてンのよ。六中は区内で二番目に強えンだけど」
lines.english: “So then the third guy to show was this Mishima dude, fifth strongest at Fourth Middle, but a month before that I dropped Triple-Punch Ichirou, fourth strongest at Sixth Middle, in two hits. And Sixth Middle is second strongest in the ward.”

lines.japanese: 「うるっせえ、死ねえええ！　ツノなんか要るかあああ！　ブチ殺してやらあああ、あ、あ、ああっ……うそ、やべ、やられる……あああ死ぬ死ぬ、羽田たすけて……はね、はね、羽田っ」
lines.english: “Shut up and dieee! Who needs your stupid horns?! I'll kill you, I'll— Ah. Ah. Aaaah! No, wait, shit, it's getting me... I'm dying, I'm dying! Haneda, help... Hane—Hane—Haneda!”

lines.japanese: 「森里君、逃げてていいよ。あとはおれが適当に倒しとくから」
lines.english: “You can keep running, Morisato. I'll finish it off somehow.”

lines.japanese: 「でさ？　敵がこっちからこう来ンじゃん。こうグオーって。でもそんなんもう俺読んでるわけ。だから左にかわしーの、顔面ぶちこみーの、相手ふらっとイッちゃってからのー……ハイかかと落としどーん！　つって」
lines.english: “So, right? The guy comes at me like this. All RAAARGH. But I've already read him. So I slip left, smash him in the face, he's all wobbly and out of it, and then—bam! Axe kick!”

lines.japanese: 「おっしゃ、体力全快ィー！　うおおおお、羽田ばっか危険な目に遭わせられッかあー！　いま助太刀に行くぞ、おりゃあああああ！」
lines.english: “Hell yeah, full health! Raaaagh! Like I'm gonna let Haneda take all the danger! I'm coming to back you up! Hyaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、森里君、邪魔だから隠れてていいよ」
lines.english: “Oh, Morisato, you're in the way. You can stay hidden.”

lines.japanese: 「つって、そっからは大輔レジェンド幕開けっつって、学校中の女がキャア～つって、ま俺、童貞捨てたの１６ンときつって、あれ、ワタライン初体験いくつッつったっけ。ゴメ忘れちった、１３つったっけ？　１２？」
lines.english: “And from there, that's the dawn of the Daisuke legend. Every girl in school goes ‘Eeeek!’ and I'm like, yeah, lost my virginity at sixteen. Wait, how old did Watarain say she was her first time? Sorry, forgot. Thirteen? Twelve?”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ森里君、お大事に」
lines.english: “Well, take care, Morisato.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、じゃあな」
lines.english: “Sure. Later.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人先輩、わっしみ～！　ワタラインもお疲れチャンでぃーっす！　こんど友達紹介してねー！　性格どーでもいいから、顔かわいくて胸おっきい子ー！」
lines.english: “Hayato, wassuuup! Later, Watarain! Introduce me to one of your friends next time! Personality doesn't matter. Just make her cute with big tits!”

lines.japanese: 「最悪だ……久しぶりに最悪な男を見た……」
lines.english: “The worst... It's been a long time since I saw a man that awful...”

lines.japanese: 森里君の病室を出たあと、僕は渡来さんに謝った。
lines.english: After we left Morisato's room, I apologized to Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「なんか、さっきはふたりで勝手に盛りあがっちゃってごめんね」
lines.english: “Um, sorry we got carried away talking to each other in there.”

lines.japanese: 「そういえば渡来さん、土門君とずっと楽しそうに話してたけど、どんな話してたの？　面白いよね、彼」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, you and Domon seemed to be having fun talking the whole time. What were you discussing? He's amusing, isn't he?”

lines.japanese: 「……気にして」
lines.english: “...Worry about it.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「うん……気にして……」
lines.english: “Yes... Worry about it...”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに？」
lines.english: “Huh? About what?”

lines.japanese: 「いい加減すこしは気にかけろッつってんだよ小僧」
lines.english: “I'm telling you to show a little damn consideration already, boy.”

lines.japanese: 「す、すみません……」
lines.english: “S-Sorry...”

lines.japanese: そのあと僕はこってりしぼられた。
lines.english: She gave me a thorough scolding afterward.

lines.japanese: デリカシーのない自分が情けない。
lines.english: I was ashamed of how thoughtless I could be.

lines.japanese: それはそれとして、渡来さんに本気で怒られるのはちょっとぞくぞくした。
lines.english: That aside, having Watarai genuinely angry with me sent a small thrill down my spine.
